To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We present a novel data-driven approach to image synthesis that is not limited to a single dataset, and can generate arbitrarily high resolution images by combining shapes and parts.

(1) simple, classic computer vision tools can be used to generate high quality images from semantic labelmaps; (2) these simple, classic tools can also be used to synthesize arbitrarily high-resolution images, and (3) by combining the two, one can generate an exponentially larger set of viable candidates, which can be used to enable user-driven content creation.

(a) a simple, data driven approach to image synthesis can be used to synthesize high resolution, realistic images from semantic labelmaps (b) the approach can be used to generate an exponentially large number of candidate outputs, and (c) the approach is not limited to training data distributions, and can generate images from a variety of domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can we synthesize in the wild images, given only a semantic label map?
the question of whether it is possible to create a system that is capable of generating images of arbitrary complexity and diversity from a small library of exemplar images.
developing a simple, yet powerful, approach for image synthesis that can be used to create a wide range of plausible, but diverse, images from a single input label map.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated that a simple, data driven approach can outperform learning based approaches on a diverse set of images.
this paper presents a new approach for synthesizing images of real-world scenes from semantic label maps that does not require any training data.
this paper presents an interesting approach to synthesizing images from label maps that is simple, efficient, and flexible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to show that simple tools can outperform recent deep learning approaches on image synthesis, while at the same time providing a platform for user interaction and content creation.
we have developed a simple, yet powerful system for image synthesis that can be used to generate images in the wild, with no learning, and no limitations on the type of images that can be created.
we are able to synthesize images from semantic label map in a data driven way, which is a very important step for image synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

simple tools for matching scene, shape, and part context can be combined to generate a large set of plausible candidate outputs, and that such an approach can outperform learning-based methods on standard image synthesis tasks.
classic tools can be used to synthesize high quality results, without the need for learning.
simple, data driven methods can achieve impressive results on challenging image synthesis tasks.
